slides.text: When my vision finally failed entirely in my mid-twenties, the world went terrifyingly dark. My biggest heartbreak wasn't losing the sunset, but losing the brilliant night sky. My boyfriend, Julian, an incredibly patient and brilliant architect, promised he would fix it. I cried, telling him he couldn't build a new sky. For weeks, he spent his evenings locked in our spare room, drilling and hammering late into the night.

On the evening of our anniversary, Julian tied a soft silk blindfold over my useless eyes and led me gently into the spare room. 'Lie down,' he whispered, guiding me to a pile of plush blankets on the floor. 'Take the blindfold off.' I did, staring into the familiar, heavy blackness. Then, I heard the click of a switch, and the ceiling above me began to hum with a gentle mechanical whir.

Suddenly, thousands of tiny, warm points of light dropped down on invisible strings, stopping just inches above my face. 'Reach out,' Julian said softly. I raised my trembling hands, brushing my fingertips against the delicate, glowing bulbs. He had physically mapped out the entire galaxy for me to touch. 'You can't see the sky anymore,' he whispered, pressing a kiss to my forehead, 'so I brought the stars down to you.'
